ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the circuit diagram is a battery, above the battery is connected an ammeter A, and then a 20Ω resistor is connected in series. After the 20Ω resistor, it reaches a node on the upper wire; from this node downward there is a branch that connects to the bottom wire through a 15Ω resistor. The upper wire continues to the right, and on the right side there is another branch downward through a 30Ω resistor; the lower end of the 30Ω resistor is connected to the bottom wire through the switch S at the bottom. Reasoning: When switch S is closed, the lower end of the 30Ω resistor is connected to the bottom wire, so the 30Ω resistor and the 15Ω resistor are both connected between the same pair of nodes: the upper ends are at the same upper node, and the lower ends are at the same bottom node. Resistors connected between the same pair of nodes are in a parallel relationship, and the potential differences across parallel components are equal. Therefore, the potential difference across the 15Ω resistor is equal to the potential difference across the 30Ω resistor.

From that junction one branch goes down through the 15 Ω resistor to the bottom wire, and another branch goes right and down through the 30 Ω resistor; when the switch at the bottom is closed, the lower end of the 30 Ω branch is connected to the same bottom wire as the lower end of the 15 Ω branch. Then use the text prompt to focus on the potential difference across the 15 Ω resistor and ask which other resistor shares it. Since the 15 Ω and 30 Ω resistors are connected between the same two nodes when the switch is closed, they are in parallel, so their potential differences are equal. Answer: the 30 Ω resistor.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a circuit with a battery, ammeter, and 20 Ω resistor in series before a split into two possible return paths: one path through the 15 Ω resistor and another path through the 30 Ω resistor whose lower connection is completed only when switch S is closed. The battery, ammeter, 20 Ω resistor, and ideal connecting wires are common to both loop descriptions; the only differing element is 15 Ω versus 30 Ω.
